newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa shortlists Telkom privatisation partners.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa shortlists Telkom privatisation partners.

text.p: South African post and telecommunications minister Jay Naidoo said on Thursday that seven international companies had been shortlisted to take a strategic equity stake of 20 to 30 percent in state-run utility Telkom.
A further 10 percent of Telkom would also be made available to black economic empowerment groups.
The following companies had satisfied initial selection criteria and been selected to proceed in a due diligence exercise, he told a news conference in Cape Town:
Naidoo said there were no preferred bidders and his ministry would encourage the formation of consortia between parties of complementary strength.
The shortlisted parties would also be able to introduce additional players into their consortia subject to them satisfying the ministry's selection criteria.
Government had previously issued a list of prospective partners which had also included British Telecommunications and Bell Atlantic Corp.
The Telkom deal is South Africa's first major privatisation project and is seen as a lithmus test of the government's commitment to sell off state assets.
